evidence_items.summary: Introduction. With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence technology, large language models (LLMs) are expected to play an important role in improving access to and the use of library collections. This study constructs and develops a generative conversational large language model tailored specifically to epitaphs, overcoming traditional research paths and systems of digitisation. Method. Based on the Chinese epitaph database built by the Zhejiang University Library and some commercial epitaph databases, an epitaph generative dialogue large language model was constructed using Doubao as the base model through pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and other full process trainings. Analysis. This study used human evaluation, in which experts, researchers, or general users assessed the quality of model-generated outputs. The evaluation included the epitaphs of Cui Yi, Liu Yi, and Lihua in the Tang dynasty. Results. The model successfully performed intelligent interpretation of epitaphs, automatic information extraction, and other knowledge-based services, thereby providing new ideas for constructing an ancient literature corpus from excavated materials represented by epitaphs. Conclusion. A large-scale domain-specific foundational model tailored for library applications was successfully developed. The study offers innovative approaches for processing historical texts and suggests new directions for AI integration in library knowledge systems.
evidence_items.title: Building a domain-specific large language model for Chinese ancient books: a case study on epitaph modelling

evidence_items.summary: Abstract This chapter provides a foundational account of artificial intelligence for the book’s later analysis of key concepts of insurance and insurance law. It traces AI’s development from Turing and early expert systems to modern machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and general-purpose generative models, while distinguishing narrow AI, AGI, and ASI. It explains core AI techniques, the lifecycle of AI systems from data collection to post-deployment monitoring, and the main risks arising at each stage, including bias, opacity, hallucinations, security failures, deployment error, and feedback loops. The chapter also highlights the central role of data quality and governance, and surveys emerging standards and regulatory frameworks, particularly the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC standards, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Overall, it argues that understanding AI’s technical architecture is essential for assessing accountability, liability, and the evolving role of insurance in managing AI-related harms.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence: The Technology

evidence_items.summary: Circadian phase can be inferred from gene expression when sample collection times are unavailable, but the available methods have not been systematically compared. We compared ten unsupervised phase inference methods and two clock-gene baselines on 25 datasets with reference times (16 real datasets from five studies and 9 simulations). The primary measure was the aligned circular mean absolute error (MAE), with a permutation test for significance, circular correlations and gene-level reconstruction of rhythmicity, acrophase and amplitude were secondary outcomes. CHIRAL had the lowest mean MAE (1.80 h, 95% confidence interval 1.21-2.97 h from resampling study families). The two clock-gene baselines (2.15 and 2.20 h) were next, followed by TEMPO, CYCLOPS and CYCLOPS 2.0 (2.49-2.80 h), and the confidence intervals of these six overlapped substantially. The other six methods had mean errors of 3.91-4.86 h, compared with 5.08-5.23 h for permuted phases. Accuracy depended on the dataset and on the strength of clock-gene rhythms, and, for several methods, on the random seed and the adjustment for batch or covariates. When the inferred phases were used to analyse gene rhythms in 22 datasets, the four leading methods identified rhythmic genes with a median ROC AUC of 0.64-0.70 and recovered gene acrophases with a median error of 0.18-0.64 h. In two mouse datasets without collection times, agreement with external reference acrophases differed between methods and tissues.
evidence_items.title: A Benchmark of Unsupervised Circadian Phase Inference Methods for Bulk Transcriptomic Data

evidence_items.summary: Background: Type-B aortic dissection requires separation of the true and false lumina in heterogeneous, anisotropic CTA. A topology term may reduce fragmentation, but its reproducibility must be tested under a fixed case split and independent native-grid evaluation. Methods: We used the public Graz type-B aortic dissection CTA collection (40 cases; CC BY 4.0) and froze a 28/6/6 case split for training, development, and held-out testing. A compact 2.5-D U-Net trained with cross-entropy plus multiclass Dice was compared with the identical model augmented by a fixed-weight (0.5) differentiable slice-level soft clDice term. Two training seeds were run for each arm. All 40 cases passed the NRRD audit; predictions for six held-out cases were restored to their native grids and scored with case-level 3-D voxel-grid Dice, voxel-grid morphological clDice, 6-connected component counts, physical-volume error, and 2,000-resample case-level paired bootstrap intervals. Results: With seed 20261007, topology-minus-baseline differences were -0.028 (95% CI -0.053 to -0.004) for true-lumen Dice, +0.032 (-0.006 to +0.096) for true-lumen voxel-grid clDice, +0.071 (+0.037 to +0.103) for false-lumen Dice, and +0.073 (+0.048 to +0.103) for false-lumen voxel-grid clDice. With seed 20261008, the corresponding differences were -0.040 (-0.065 to -0.018), +0.013 (-0.034 to +0.071), -0.099 (-0.187 to -0.004), and -0.058 (-0.124 to -0.001). Descriptive pooled means over 12 case rows per arm were true-lumen Dice 0.577 for topology versus 0.611 for baseline and false-lumen Dice 0.409 versus 0.422; these pooled rows are not independent cases. Conclusions: Under this fixed six-case test split, the corrected slice-level topology term did not produce a consistent benefit. True-lumen Dice was lower in both seeds, while false-lumen effects reversed direction between seeds; topology-clDice changes were small and/or interval-crossing.
evidence_items.title: A public-data reproducibility benchmark of a 2.5-D U-Net with a slice-level topology term for type-B aortic dissection segmentation

organizations: Independent Researcher
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Reported accuracies on a widely used four-class brain tumor MRI benchmark routinely exceed 98%, but the released split discards patient identity. We content-matched tumor images to their figshare source and recovered identifiers for 4586 images from 233 patients. Of 906 tumor test images, 761 were traceable; every one belonged to a patient represented in training. Separately, 216 of 1311 test images were pixel-identical to training images. Removing duplicates did not reduce accuracy (99.22% to 99.42%), whereas five-fold patient-disjoint cross-validation yielded 95.19% overall and 93.68% on tumor classes. On the same 761 images, accuracy fell from 99.12% when the patient appeared in training to 93.60% when absent, increasing the error rate 7.3-fold. A matched random-fold control attributed 2.73 of the 4.03 percentage-point gap to patient grouping rather than the change in evaluation design; the class without patient identifiers changed negligibly despite relaxed proxy grouping. These results show that the released split measures recognition of additional slices from previously seen patients, not generalization to unseen patients. We release the recovered patient map, fixed folds, predictions, and analysis code.
evidence_items.title: Complete Patient-Level Leakage Among Traceable Images in a Widely Used Brain Tumor MRI Benchmark

organizations: Research Group of Advanced Control Systems, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Rambla Sant Nebridi 22, 08222 Terrassa, Spain
evidence_items.summary: Water-infrastructure digitalization increasingly couples hydraulics with sensing, communication, artificial intelligence (AI), and supervisory control, while digital twins support operational decisions. This article combines a critical narrative review with structured full-text evidence mapping of 50 water cyber-physical systems (CPS) studies and an accompanying reproducible Water Distribution Testbed (WDT) benchmark case study. The review synthesizes model-based, data-driven, and physically informed methods across detection, localization, mitigation, and recovery, distinguishing anomaly evidence, cyber attribution, and closed-loop resilience. The WDT case study compares nominal-only detectors and alarm policies under a common chronological protocol. Across five primary neural runs, cumulative policies increase sample-level recall but sustain alarms and detect fewer event onsets than the fixed-threshold policy. These numerical findings characterize the declared protocol and evaluated records; they do not establish a general ranking of detection algorithms. They motivate interpreting classification metrics alongside event performance and held-out nominal alarm burden. Priorities include trustworthy digital-twin updating, causal localization, uncertainty-aware intervention, independent validation, and verified recovery for intelligent water-infrastructure operation.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Digital Twins, and Cyber-Resilience in Water Distribution Systems: A Critical Narrative Review with a WDT Benchmark Case Study

evidence_items.summary: Purpose: This paper examines WebMCP, a proposed browser-native web platform standard that lets websites expose explicit, schema-described tools to large language model agents, as an alternative to actuation, in which an agent simulates the clicks, keystrokes, and navigation a human would perform. Methodology: The paper analyzes WebMCP, incubated within the World Wide Web Consortium's Web Machine Learning Community Group and implemented as an origin trial in the Chrome browser beginning with Chrome 149. We describe WebMCP's architecture, including the browser-mediated JavaScript interface navigator.modelContext and a declarative HTML annotation form, and its relationship to Anthropic's Model Context Protocol; analyze its security and permission model; place it within a comparative design-space taxonomy alongside DOM automation, computer-use agents, and server-side Model Context Protocol integrations; and examine the emerging standardization landscape, including browser vendor positions and adjacent efforts such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol. A generalized use case illustrates how a composite retail website might expose search, filtering, and checkout tools under this model. All sources and data referenced in this manuscript are dated on or before June 30, 2026. Findings: WebMCP allows a website to register tools that an agent invokes directly rather than inferring actions from pixels or DOM structure, with a security model built on origin isolation, a dedicated Permissions Policy directive, and a human-in-the-loop confirmation mechanism for consequential actions. Open problems remain in cross-site tool discovery, adversarial tool poisoning, and the evaluation of agent-web interaction quality. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: For theory, the paper contributes a comparative design-space taxonomy that positions browser-native, declarative agent integration against actuation-based and server-side approaches.
evidence_items.title: WebMCP: A Browser-Native navigator.modelContext Standard for Agentic Web Automation

evidence_items.summary: Soft porous crystals can undergo guest-induced structural transitions producing unconventional adsorption isotherms, which are valuable for gas separation and storage applications. However, the evidence for these transitions is scattered across the literature in narrative form and has not been aggregated. Here we use a large language model pipeline to mine the literature for anomalous adsorption, extracting phase-transition events together with material, adsorbate, temperature and pressure metadata and classifying each into an established behavioural class. Benchmarked against human annotation, the extraction stage attains an F1 score of 0.96. When applied at scale, the pipeline yields a curated corpus of 547 transitions across 240 distinct materials, drawn from 200 of 4,252 screened publications, which we further link to crystallographic structures. Analysis of this database shows that the principal behavioural classes, gate-opening and breathing, are distinguished by their functional response. Gate-opening frameworks transform at a significantly lower pressure than breathing frameworks (p = 3.8E-3). In contrast, no difference in pore size, void fraction, linker chemistry or metal identity was detected between the classes. Our findings argue for a functional rather than purely structural description of responsive porous materials. They also highlight the need for a community database that records the guest, temperature and pressure of every reported transition of these materials.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena

evidence_items.summary: Long-context capability has become essential for large language models (LLMs) to handle complex tasks, yet continuously expanding the context window does not remove the computational, storage, and information-selection pressures incurred at inference time. Existing work on prompt compression, KV-cache management, efficient serving, retrieval augmentation, and agent memory is usually discussed in isolation, leaving the flow of information between storage and computation insufficiently understood. This survey reframes long-context compression as a memory-management problem for allocating inference-time resources. We distinguish compute-active memory, which directly participates in model computation, from compute-inactive memory, which lies outside the computation path but can be stored, retrieved, updated, or forgotten, and we characterize offloaded KV caches, persistent prefix caches, and precomputed KV states as intermediate states on the activation path. On this basis, we formulate writing, offloading, recall, retrieval-and-injection, materialization, eviction, consolidation, and forgetting as state transitions within an information lifecycle, and introduce a budgeted cost model that places these operations in a single cost account. The resulting framework unifies short-term context compression, long-term memory management, and the transitions between them, and shows that the central challenge is not merely reducing information volume but deciding which information should participate in costly inference, when, and in what form. We further summarize evaluation dimensions, benchmark gaps, and open challenges, and argue that future research should move from static, pointwise compression toward dynamic, governable, lifecycle-aware memory management.
evidence_items.title: From Long Context to Selective Memory:A Survey of Memory-Centric Compression for Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Root-cause analysis (RCA) in large-scale distributed systems is challenging because a single symptom can cross service, data, configuration, compute, and organizational boundaries. Responders must assemble incomplete evidence and coordinate experts who hold different parts of the causal path. Generic language-model agents do not solve this problem through tool access alone: they can use stale or mistimed context, interpret failed queries as absent symptoms, report unsupported system state, and overload observability services designed for human-paced use. We present Diviner (Domain-Informed Verifiable Incident Navigation through Evidence and Review), an agentic RCA system operating at Meta and organized around a four-stage reliability lifecycle. Encode combines a large corpus of reviewed incidents with service-owner expertise to produce scoped, versioned skills, workflows, typed tools, and an incident knowledge graph. Execute uses an adaptive Lead and context-isolated workers to apply relevant knowledge to point-in-time evidence and maintain evidence-linked hypotheses. Evaluate compares saved investigation trajectories with responder-reviewed outcomes to measure exact cause, useful direction, and Groundedness. Adapt uses recurring gaps and on-call feedback to derive focused operational- knowledge updates, admitting them only after replay, quality checks, and owner approval.
evidence_items.title: Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure

evidence_items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves a student language model by training on its own generated trajectories with supervision from a stronger teacher. However, when conditioned on student-generated prefixes, the teacher can favor invalid continuations that violate the question's premises, causing OPD to encourage erroneous reasoning steps. As a remedy, we introduce Condition-Contrastive Extrapolated On-Policy Distillation (CCE-OPD), which makes teacher supervision sensitive to question conditions. CCE-OPD incorporates (1) a fixed-prefix comparison in which the same frozen teacher evaluates the complete question and a counterpart with a selected condition masked, and (2) a bounded log-probability contrast that reweights the teacher distribution into an auxiliary distillation target. On 200 diagnostic reasoning states, condition contrast reduces the rate of preferring invalid continuations from 27.0% to 16.0%. Extensive experiments across six mathematical benchmarks show that CCE-OPD improves avg@8 over OPD by an average of 1.60 and 1.95 percentage points when distilling Qwen3-8B into 0.6B and 1.7B students, respectively. It also achieves the strongest results on four transfer benchmarks.
evidence_items.title: Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for election information, yet little is known about how external web content shapes the political information they present. Generative engine optimization (GEO) rewrites web content to improve its visibility in generated responses. To investigate its potential risks in voting scenarios (VoteGEO), we introduce VoteGEO-Bench, a benchmark covering the 2024 U.S. presidential election and the 2026 Japanese House of Representatives election, combining election-related queries, historical webpages, and voter personas. We first analyze sources cited by generative engines and find that many citations come from lower-cost owned and open-platform sources, while some webpages remain visible across days. We then evaluate 11 rewriting strategies in 4 categories, examining target specification, effectiveness across engines and elections, and the role of voter personas. Rewriting without specifying a target rarely increases target exposure, whereas target-specified rewriting more often does. Strategies that improve page organization or strengthen a position through argumentation yield greater gains than adding supporting evidence or changing wording. For the two strongest strategies, gains remain broadly positive across evaluated U.S. personas, but persona conditioning shows no consistent effect on these gains. Explicit partisan identities can create baseline exposure gaps larger than the gain from rewriting one webpage. When partisanship is implicit in the voter profile, baseline shifts depend on how strongly the engine responds to that signal.
evidence_items.title: VoteGEO-Bench: Measuring the Impact of Generative Engine Optimization on Electoral Visibility

evidence_items.summary: Large language models increasingly rely on external memory to answer queries grounded in long-horizon histories such as multi-session dialogues and lengthy documents. However, existing memory methods often optimize retrieval and memory construction separately, without a shared reward space for evaluating search, writing, and stopping decisions. To address this, we propose All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem), which organizes these operations as transitions over a shared evidence state and directly evaluates the semantic quality of each action in a unified reward space. AiO-Mem compiles heterogeneous histories into source-traceable multi-view events, providing a shared substrate for retrieval and memory writing. A unified memory policy actor then rolls out complete interaction trajectories over this shared evidence state. A separate trajectory-conditioned process reward model is trained through evidence-grounded supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level DPO to assign process scores to the collected trajectories. These scores are aggregated into an action-balanced trajectory reward and used by Process-Aligned DAPO (PA-DAPO) to optimize the memory policy. Across long-context memory benchmarks, AiO-Mem consistently improves answer accuracy over both static memory systems and RL-trained memory agents.
evidence_items.title: All-in-One Memory: Process-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Memory Agents

evidence_items.summary: Agentic large language models have been documented to lose reasoning capability when placed inside a harness, the software that mediates their observations and actions. To reconcile these losses, we introduce AutoOnboarder, an autonomous system that adapts an agent to a task the way a trainer onboards a new employee. It places the agent under the supervision of an intelligent ``Onboarder''coding agent, which iteratively tailors its foundation model, prompt, and harness source code to simultaneously improve performance and decrease cost. Like a real onboarding process, the Onboarder is only given tens of examples, and all evaluation data is isolated on a separate virtual machine to prevent leakage. We report the lessons learned from building and testing AutoOnboarder on genomic-sequencing prior authorization form submission. Autonomously onboarded agents are able to match or exceed the performance of a Gemini 3.5 Flash baseline at up to 29$\times$ lower costs. However, these agents remain imperfect, and the Onboarding process varies greatly in terms of final performance. We conclude that future Onboarding systems require a robust environment for the Onboarder, including a structured thought interface, (controlled) internet access, and a wide model search space.
evidence_items.title: AutoOnboarder: Autonomously Onboarding LLM Agents

evidence_items.summary: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) relies on the timely identification of emerging threats, enabling organizations and security analysts to support situational awareness and decision-making. Social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) have become valuable CTI sources because vulnerabilities and attack activities are often discussed there before appearing in formal reports. However, the rapid growth of cybersecurity discussions on social media has created more content than domain experts can realistically review and annotate, making labeled data a major bottleneck for developing supervised learning approaches. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as weak annotators in other domains, their effectiveness for cybersecurity tweet classification and downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models (PLMs) remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose a Teacher-Student weak supervision framework in which a selected LLM serves as a Teacher to generate weak labels for unlabeled cybersecurity tweets, enabling the training of cybersecurity-specific PLMs without large-scale manual annotation. Experimental results show that PLMs trained solely on LLM-generated labels consistently achieve F1 scores above 0.92, remaining within 3 percentage points of fully human-supervised models across all evaluated architectures. These findings suggest that LLM-based weak annotation offers a practical alternative for constructing cybersecurity-specific training data when expert annotation resources are limited.
evidence_items.title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework

evidence_items.summary: Detailed captions transfer visual information into vision-language model supervision, but quality is easily conflated with length: long single-pass outputs still miss small objects, text, and spatial relations or promote uncertain observations into confident claims. We formulate fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, in which a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget and converts it into reusable supervision. ZoomCap uses a draft caption to route conditional knowledge retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage-gap recovery, and adaptive visual zooming, allocating deeper crops only to the most complex eligible region, deriving spatial relations from grounded geometry, and fusing non-duplicate evidence. We also introduce FactCycle, which scores caption-derived atomic claims on two blind anchors--source image (truthfulness) and reconstruction (realizability)--separating fabrication from generator loss claim by claim; human and multi-judge comparisons complement this fact-level view. Against Qwen3.5-397B-A17B captions, ZoomCap achieves an 81.9% human tie-adjusted preference score with a teacher over 10x smaller, and FactCycle counts 52.4 transferred claims per image vs. 31.5 for ScaleCap. The evidence also transfers: in continual pre-training, ZoomCap-450K improves the 11-benchmark average by 1.31-2.38 points over the strongest competing corpus and Ling-Tiny-VL-v3 gains 1.4 points on a production document/OCR monitor suite (1.5 on perception) at 60B tokens; in medical pre-training, 2.64M ZoomCap-captioned images improve five VQA benchmarks by 3.04 points (vs. 1.76 for same-image Gemini-3.1-Pro captions).
evidence_items.title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer

evidence_items.summary: GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) provide the primary satellite gravimetry observations of terrestrial water storage (TWS) variations from 2002 onwards. However, continuously improving global hydrological models often span substantially longer periods, while their validation in the pre-GRACE era remains challenging and requires complementary observations or long-term gravity field reconstructions. The validation can be conducted by combining information from GRACE with other geodetic techniques, such as Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR) and Doppler Orbitography and Radiopositioning Integrated by Satellite (DORIS). An important question, however, is to what extent hydrological model assessments depend on the choice of long-term gravity field reconstruction used as a benchmark.To address this question, we use our recently developed long-term SLR+GRACE gravity field reconstruction, which extends GRACE information back to 1995 by combining the complementary strengths of SLR and GRACE. The lowest-degree spherical harmonics are constrained directly by SLR, while intermediate and higher degrees incorporate GRACE-derived temporal and spatial information to provide gravity field solutions up to degree and order 60 also for the pre-GRACE period. We compare this reconstruction with an independently developed SLR+DORIS gravity field solution over the common period 1995–2022. Their applicability as long-term hydrological benchmarks is evaluated for the 100 largest river basins using TWS estimates from OS LISFLOOD and the Land Surface Discharge Model (LSDM), which has been widely used in geodetic applications for nearly two decades. Model benchmark agreement is quantified using the centered Kling–Gupta Efficiency (cKGE) and Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE). In addition, differences in NSE between OS LISFLOOD and LSDM (ΔNSE) are compared between the SLR+GRACE and SLR+DORIS benchmarks to assess whether both gravity field reconstructions lead to the same qualitative ranking of the hydrological models.The results show that OS LISFLOOD is generally more consistent with the gravimetric benchmarks than LSDM, particularly in large tropical and subtropical basins. For the SLR+GRACE reconstruction, median cKGE values are 0.59 for OS LISFLOOD and 0.50 for LSDM for detrended TWS, and 0.41 and 0.23, respectively, for interannual variability. More importantly, SLR+GRACE and SLR+DORIS yield the same sign of ΔNSE in 70.7% of cases for detrended TWS and 64.3% for interannual variability. The median absolute difference in ΔNSE between the two benchmarks increases from 0.12 to 0.20, indicating that model assessment is largely robust to benchmark choice, but becomes more sensitive at interannual timescales.In addition, degree-1 coefficients and the corresponding geocenter motion were reconstructed from the SLR+GRACE solution for 1995–2023. This extends the reconstructed geocenter series into the pre-GRACE era, fills the gap between GRACE and GRACE-FO, and complements our long-term gravity field reconstruction with degree-1 information.
evidence_items.title: Beyond GRACE: Benchmarking Global Hydrological Models Back to the 1990s with Satellite Laser Ranging

evidence_items.summary: Instruction-following language models can comply with requests that conflict with intended behaviors and safety alignment. We introduce a training-free weight-editing approach for reducing compliance with targeted undesirable instructions. Our method needs only forward passes on a small set of prompt pairs per target behavior, and because the edit is stored in the model's weights, changing or deleting instructions in the prompt cannot undo the weight modification. We evaluate the approach on two target harmful behaviors across five instruction-tuned models: instructed falsehood and instructed sexism. On two instructed-lying benchmarks, it improves mean honest response rates by 6.2 and 4.6 percentage points over the strongest alternative, significantly on three of the five models and within noise on the other two. In a controlled study of seven prompt formats, it maintains higher honest-response rates than single-layer activation steering when orders to lie arrive in single-turn formats not used to construct the edit. For instructed sexism, it reduces the mean sexist-response rate from 57.9% to 24.3%; combining the edit with a fairness prompt reduces it further to 11.9%. These results establish our contrast-based weight editing approach as an effective training-free intervention in two distinct behavioral domains, supporting its use both independently and alongside prompt-based safeguards.
evidence_items.title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing

evidence_items.summary: Forecasting short-term movements in financial markets remains challenging because market prices are influenced by rapidly changing economic conditions, investor sentiment, and volatility. While machine-learning methods have demonstrated promise for financial forecasting, many forecasting tools remain difficult for non-technical users to interpret and often provide predictions without contextual explanations. This paper presents StockForecastGenie Pro, a volatility-aware machine-learning decision-support system designed to forecast short-horizon movements in major United States equity indices while providing transparent and interpretable signals. The system forecasts future index levels, point gains, and percentage returns for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average using a stacked ensemble of machine-learning models. Forecast outputs are combined with market-volatility information derived from the CBOE V olatility Index (VIX) to generate plain-language signals ranging from Strong Negative to Strong Positive. The platform also incorporates confidence estimates, simple benchmark comparisons, and broader market context to support user interpretation. A rolling historical evaluation was conducted, and results indicate that forecasting performance improves substantially as forecast horizon increases. At the five-day horizon, the stacked ensemble achieved directional accuracy of 73.2% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 70.9% for the S&P 500. Compared with a no-change benchmark, the system reduced forecast error by approximately 24.3% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 22.4% for the S&P 500. The results demonstrate that machine-learning ensembles can provide meaningful improvements over simple forecasting approaches while maintaining interpretability for research, educational, and decision-support applications.
evidence_items.title: StockForecastGenie Pro: A Volatility-Aware Machine Learning Decision-Support System for Short-Horizon Equity Index Forecasting

evidence_items.summary: Point cloud upsampling is essential for 3D applications but remains challenging due to sparse, under-constrained observations. Multi-view images can resolve geometric ambiguity, but existing multi-modal methods do not fully exploit visual cues. We propose ControlFlow3D, a framework that distills knowledge from pretrained foundation models into a lightweight generation network during training, enabling strong performance without multi-view images available at test time. Specifically, our method performs conditional flow matching in a structured latent space defined by a frozen 3D encoder. Multi-view image tokens and 3D latent tokens are jointly clustered into shared prototypes via unsupervised soft KMeans; the resulting prototypes guide the flow trajectory through velocity control and are aligned by a consistency loss that progressively transfers image knowledge into the base network. A Mamba-based geometry decoder then maps latent features to dense coordinates with linear complexity. We also construct ShapeNetPU, a 35K-object multi-modal benchmark that is 31 times larger than prior datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and its strong generalization capability.
evidence_items.title: ControlFlow3D: Distilling Multi-View Knowledge into Latent Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms are increasingly embedded within enterprise Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud systems, introducing critical security vulnerabilities related to prompt injection, inference abuse, and sensitive data leakage. These risks are amplified in cloud-native environments where distributed architectures complicate centralized control enforcement. This article proposes a layered security architecture that operationalizes the Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture (SABSA) framework alongside active DevSecOps engineering pipelines. To bridge the gap between abstract risk governance and technical implementation, we implement an empirical validation framework on an AWS environment using a local DistilGPT-2 instance executing simulated adversarial vectors. Unlike existing qualitative security models, our architecture introduces empirical performance benchmarks evaluated against the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) and structured zero trust parameters. Controlled experimental assessments demonstrate that integrating multitier string pattern-matching logic achieves a robust absolute mitigation rate against direct prompt injection payloads while bounding inference processing runtime overhead strictly under 41.6 ms. Continuous deployment validations executed via IaC Checkov scanning demonstrate robust multilayered architectural traceability, satisfying rigorous verification metrics necessary for scalable cloud-based AI platform assurance.
evidence_items.title: Enhancing DevSecOps Practices for Secure AI Platforms Using SABSA

evidence_items.summary: A reproducible check of two common claims about AI agent leaderboards, on 3,300 public Terminal-Bench 4.0 runs (10 configurations, 66 tasks, 5 trials each). Removing the 30 tasks flagged as defective by Epoch AI does not change the ranking beyond noise, and ranking by pass^5 instead of pass@1 does not either. Agents do differ in how correlated their repeats are on Terminal-Bench 2.0, and much of that difference sits in the 28 tasks the benchmark later changed. With 66 tasks, pass@1 differences within about 9.5 points are ties. Every result is recomputed from raw trials by reproduce.py with fixed seeds. Also includes a tool to run the same tests on any leaderboard with per-trial data.

evidence_items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used to interpret religious, educational, and culturally sensitive visual content, yet their reliability on citation verification remains underexplored. We introduce Visual Sanad, a controlled benchmark for testing whether VLMs falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions when the same quote-reference pair is rendered under different visual framings. The benchmark contains 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions ranging from plain text to decorative and authority-framed layouts. All quote-reference pairs were source-checked and human-audited before rendering. Across 24 full model-prompt runs, we observe a sharp capability split. Proprietary API-served VLMs range from near-perfect citation verification to moderate false acceptance, whereas recent open-weight VLMs often show weak discrimination and default to VALID on most images. De-biased prompting can reduce false acceptance, but often by shifting the decision threshold toward INVALID rather than by producing strong citation discrimination. Visual Sanad therefore exposes a culturally grounded multimodal factuality failure: fluent VLMs may treat displayed religious citations as self-authenticating unless they have strong citation-verification ability.
evidence_items.title: Visual Sanad: Auditing Vision-Language Models for False Acceptance of Qur'anic Citations

evidence_items.summary: An AI data center is committed years before it draws a watt: a few discrete choices (grid or on-site gas, evaporative or dry cooling, which county to file in) fix its capital, water draw, and carbon path, and LLMs are now asked to help screen them with no test of whether they track what each commitment rules out. We introduce DCBench-440, with two arms reported separately: 200 generative questions over STRIPS worlds for five US deal archetypes, with search-verified gold answers and no tested shortcut above 12% on any question type, and 240 multiple-choice questions grounded in quoted site records, emission equations, and stated scenarios. Across open-weight deployments, accuracy spans 12.5-71.5% (generative) and 58.3-92.5% (multiple choice). One skill fails everywhere: asked to list every action available at a decision gate, no model exceeds 4.0% exact match. The strongest list 72-85% of the actions that would change the project's state but omit most permitted actions that change nothing; with those excused, the best exact match is still 24%. Code, data, and other materials are available upon request.
evidence_items.title: Watts If? A Benchmark for Counterfactual Reasoning About the AI Data Center Buildout

evidence_items.summary: Residential design aims to transform existing homes into functional living spaces while satisfying diverse design preferences and physical constraints. However, existing floorplan generation methods typically assume empty building boundaries as input, whereas renovation requires reasoning over existing floorplans. Furthermore, floorplan renovation and furniture layout are commonly addressed as separate tasks, overlooking their inherent spatial dependency. Consequently, practical residential design must preserve immutable structural components while transforming editable spatial elements. It must also optimize furniture placement under design objectives and physical constraints. To address these challenges, we formulate residential design as a design-point-guided conditional generation task and propose RenoLayout, a framework that translates a pre-design residential state together with a design-point set into an executable Geometry-as-Code program. To enable controllable supervision, we construct a Design Map comprising 123 fine-grained design points covering structural renovation and furniture layout. We further introduce Difference-Grounded Design-Point Annotation to derive design-point sets automatically from before--after design pairs with VLM-based consistency verification. RenoLayout is trained using a three-stage CPT--SFT--RL pipeline, progressively improving spatial reasoning, instruction following, and constraint compliance. We also introduce the RenoLayout Benchmark, a set of 200 real-world before--after renovation cases with complete furniture layouts. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first benchmark for unified residential design. These cases include design-critical structural and building-service constraints.
evidence_items.title: RenoLayout: Unified Floorplan Renovation and Furniture Layout for Constraint-Aware Residential Design

evidence_items.summary: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.
evidence_items.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints

evidence_items.summary: Repository-scale refactoring requires coding agents to propagate a single change across many interdependent files without altering program behavior, yet to our knowledge no existing harness isolates the design choices that determine agent success on this task. We present RefactorPlatform, an open-source evaluation harness that holds the environment fixed and varies each design axis explicitly: model backbone (via OpenRouter and GitHub Copilot CLI), execution regime (baseline, retrieval-augmented, and multi-agent), and prompt specificity. Each run executes in an isolated workspace with live terminal streaming, per-task logging of tokens, diffs, and transcripts, AST-based verification, and exportable telemetry for audit and reproduction. Demonstrating the platform on 100 multi-file RefactorBench tasks across four model families, we illustrate the analyses it supports: AST-aware chunking outperforms naive token-window chunking by 25-30 percentage points (pp) across prompt modes, whereas naive retrieval falls below the retrieval-free baseline; a lean retrieval-augmented single agent (86%) beats the sub-agent configuration we evaluated (66%) on matched tasks with no task passing under delegation that fails under retrieval; and retrieval's accuracy gains absorb its token overhead, leaving cost per successful refactoring unchanged. RefactorPlatform is open-sourced to make refactoring-agent evaluation reproducible and auditable.
evidence_items.title: RefactorPlatform: An Open-Source Harness for Controlled Evaluation of Repository-Scale Refactoring Agents

evidence_items.summary: As large language models and AI agents become the primary consumers of search results, document set quality determines the upper bound of downstream generation. Yet existing evaluation systems remain confined to scoring documents independently and aggregating via nDCG, ignoring inter-document interactions (redundancy, conflict, complementarity) and unable to answer what makes one document set better than another. To address these issues, we propose a complete evaluate-diagnose-optimize framework. We design SetwiseEvalKit, a three-level, nine-dimension document set evaluation benchmark covering both short-form and long-form scenarios, comprising approximately 28K high-quality evaluation rubrics. We systematically evaluate 12 rerankers: even the best method achieves no more than 45% coverage, cross-document coordination dimensions are universally weak, and no single method maintains top performance across both settings. Building on this, we propose Rubric4Setwise, a training-free method that converts rubric-based evaluation criteria into document set selection signals, achieving the best downstream generation performance with fewer documents and search rounds. It is the only method that maintains state-of-the-art results across both scenarios, validating the effectiveness of closing the loop from evaluation to optimization.
evidence_items.title: Beyond Relevance-Centric Retrieval: Rubric-Oriented Document Set Selection and Ranking

evidence_items.summary: Video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general and long-form video understanding, yet their ability to capture and use brief, answer-critical visual evidence remains underexplored. Momentary actions or state transitions may determine an answer while occupying only a small fraction of the video. Performance on broad video understanding tasks alone does not establish whether models can reliably identify and use this temporally localized evidence. We introduce Moment-Video, a benchmark for evaluating temporal fidelity through momentary visual event understanding. Questions are constructed around visually observable events or event sequences, requiring models to notice, count, describe, or reason about transient evidence. The benchmark contains 1,000 human-verified video-QA pairs across seven domains and 25 subcategories, covering four tasks: Temporal Occurrence, Temporal Counting, Action Description, and Temporal Reasoning. We evaluate 34 proprietary and open-source MLLMs. Under the main evaluation settings, the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves 39.6% overall accuracy, while most open-source models remain below 25%. Diagnostic analyses show that denser frame sampling improves some models, but substantial errors persist even when sampled frames cover all annotated necessary event intervals in an audited subset. Performance also declines on longer videos, suggesting additional temporal-localization challenges. By exposing these limitations, Moment-Video provides a diagnostic benchmark to guide the evaluation and development of video MLLMs that more reliably understand brief, answer-critical visual events.
evidence_items.title: Moment-Video: Diagnosing Temporal Fidelity of Video MLLMs on Momentary Visual Events

evidence_items.summary: While large vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as the perceptual backbone for embodied agents, their fundamental vision-language grounding (VLG) capability in embodied scenarios remains unexplored. We present \textbf{EPIC-Bench}, \textbf{E}mbodied \textbf{P}ercept\textbf{I}on Ben\textbf{C}hmark, a fine-grained grounding benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the VLG capabilities of VLMs in real-world embodied environments. EPIC-Bench comprises 6.6k meticulously human-annotated tuples (Image, Text, Mask) spanning three core stages of the embodied interaction pipeline: Target Localization, Navigation, and Manipulation. With 23 fine-grained tasks, multi-dimensional settings and evaluation over 80 leading VLMs, EPIC-Bench provides a diagnostic analysis.
evidence_items.title: EPIC-Bench: A Perception-Centric Benchmark for Fine-Grained Embodied Visual Grounding in Vision-Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Image editing models can modify visual content through natural language, but editing dense documents requires precise local changes amid tightly coupled text, tables, and layout. We introduce VDE Bench, an evaluation resource for studying instruction-guided editing of Chinese and English document images. VDE Bench contains 3,506 instruction-guided image editing samples, including 1,578 text-region edits and 1,928 table-region edits. The benchmark pairs editing instructions and reference images with annotated editing regions and structured OCR outputs. Its evaluation protocol combines region-level and full-page measurements to assess textual correctness, structural fidelity, and visual content preservation. By focusing on the interaction between local edits and their surrounding document context, VDE Bench complements existing visual text editing benchmarks and provides a resource for diagnosing document-specific editing failures.
evidence_items.title: VDE Bench: Evaluating The Capability of Image Editing Models to Modify Visual Documents

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) excel at natural language tasks but remain brittle in domains requiring precise logical and symbolic reasoning. Chaotic dynamical systems provide an especially demanding test because chaos is deterministic yet often misinterpreted as randomness or complexity. We introduce ChaosBench-Logic, a benchmark that evaluates LLM reasoning across 30 diverse dynamical systems using a unified first-order logic (FOL) ontology. Each system is annotated with truth assignments for 11 semantic predicates, and 621 questions are generated across seven reasoning categories, including multi-hop implications, cross-system analogies, counterfactual reasoning, bias probes, and multi-turn dialogues. We define metrics for logical accuracy, implication consistency, dialogue coherence, and contradiction, and we release an open-source evaluation pipeline. Initial experiments show that frontier LLMs such as GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and the open-source LLaMA-3 70B achieve 91-94% per-item accuracy, yet still score 0% on compositional items and exhibit fragile global coherence. Dialogue-level accuracy ranges from 53.1% (GPT-4 CoT) to 75.5% (LLaMA-3 zero-shot). ChaosBench-Logic provides a rigorous testbed for diagnosing such failures and a foundation for developing neuro-symbolic approaches that improve scientific reasoning in LLMs.
evidence_items.title: ChaosBench-Logic: A Benchmark for Logical and Symbolic Reasoning on Chaotic Dynamical Systems

evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled accurate image-based geolocation, raising serious concerns about location privacy risks in everyday social media posts. Yet, a systematic evaluation of such risks is still lacking: existing benchmarks show coarse granularity, linguistic bias, and a neglect of multimodal privacy risks. To address these gaps, we introduce KoreaGEO, the first fine-grained, multimodal, and privacy-aware benchmark for geolocation, built on Korean street views. The benchmark covers four socio-spatial clusters and nine place types with rich contextual annotations and two captioning styles that simulate real-world privacy exposure. To evaluate mainstream VLMs, we design a three-path protocol spanning image-only, functional-caption, and high-risk-caption inputs, enabling systematic analysis of localization accuracy, spatial bias, and reasoning behavior. Results show that input modality exerts a stronger influence on localization precision and privacy exposure than model scale or architecture, with high-risk captions substantially boosting accuracy. Moreover, they highlight structural prediction biases toward core cities.
evidence_items.title: AI Knows Where You Are: Exposure, Bias, and Inference in Multimodal Geolocation with KoreaGEO

evidence_items.summary: Generative large language models (LLMs) have been shown to exhibit harmful biases and stereotypes. While safety fine-tuning typically takes place in English, if at all, these models are being used by speakers of many different languages. There is existing evidence that the performance of these models is inconsistent across languages and that they discriminate based on demographic factors of the user. Motivated by this, we investigate whether the social stereotypes exhibited by LLMs differ as a function of the language used to prompt them, while controlling for cultural differences and task accuracy. To this end, we present MBBQ (Multilingual Bias Benchmark for Question-answering), a carefully curated version of the English BBQ dataset extended to Dutch, Spanish, and Turkish, which measures stereotypes commonly held across these languages. We further complement MBBQ with a parallel control dataset to measure task performance on the question-answering task independently of bias. Our results based on several open-source and proprietary LLMs confirm that some non-English languages suffer from bias more than English, even when controlling for cultural shifts. Moreover, we observe significant cross-lingual differences in bias behaviour for all except the most accurate models. With the release of MBBQ, we hope to encourage further research on bias in multilingual settings. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/Veranep/MBBQ.
evidence_items.title: MBBQ: A Dataset for Cross-Lingual Comparison of Stereotypes in Generative LLMs

evidence_items.summary: Learning from experience requires recovering reusable knowledge and determining when it applies to a new situation. We introduce OntoAct, a hypothesis-based neuro-symbolic framework built on ontological abstraction. OntoAct turns individual experiences into axioms over entity types, relations, and conditions, making their underlying patterns reusable across situations. A large language model (LLM) uses this world knowledge to propose hypotheses and actions, while a symbolic verifier assesses their supporting conditions against current observations. Verification identifies missing evidence, and new observations and intervention outcomes update hypothesis assessments and guide subsequent actions. We also introduce Tacit-FLE, a benchmark built on the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE) for diagnosing and repairing hidden faults in existing factories using inherited operational records. Its synthetic maintenance corpus distributes evidence across records, and an executed repair may leave the fault unresolved, requiring agents to reassess their diagnoses through interaction. Across Tacit-FLE, Mars, and ALFWorld, OntoAct achieves leading task performance with efficient interaction and inference.
evidence_items.title: OntoAct: Hypothesis-Based Neuro-Symbolic Agents through Ontological Abstraction

evidence_items.summary: Emesis, a complex physiological response mediated by the central and peripheral nervous systems, poses significant challenges in clinical management. This study investigated the anti-emetic potential of cinnamic acid (CA), a naturally occurring phenolic compound, through in vivo and in silico approaches. Using a copper sulfate-induced emesis model in young chicks (Gallus gallus domesticus), the anti-emetic effects of CA (10, 20, and 40 mg/kg) were evaluated and compared with standard drugs ondansetron (OND, 5 mg/kg) and domperidone (DOM, 6 mg/kg). The results demonstrated that CA significantly reduced the number of retches and prolonged the latency period in a dose-dependent manner, with the lowest dose (10 mg/kg) exhibiting the most pronounced effect (94% increase in latency, 92.85% reduction in retches). Notably, combination therapies of CA (40 mg/kg) with OND or DOM further enhanced anti-emetic efficacy, suggesting synergistic interactions. Molecular docking studies provided mechanistic insights, revealing that CA exhibited moderate binding affinity for dopamine D2 (-6.9 kcal/mol) and D3 (-6.2 kcal/mol) receptors, forming hydrophobic interactions with key residues (TRP407, PHE411, HIS349, VAL111). In contrast, CA showed minimal interaction with the 5-HT3 receptor (-5.9 kcal/mol), aligning with its potentiation of OND’s effects. Pharmacokinetic analysis via SwissADME indicated favorable drug-likeness properties for CA, including high gastrointestinal absorption (94.83%), blood-brain barrier permeability, and adherence to Lipinski’s rules. Moreover, Toxicity profiling (ProTox 3.0) predicted a high LD50 (2500 mg/kg) and low risks of mutagenicity or carcinogenicity, though mild hepatotoxicity was noted. These findings underscore CA’s potential as a multi-target anti-emetic agent, primarily via dopaminergic modulation, and its utility as an adjunct to conventional therapies.
evidence_items.title: Dataset for "Evaluation of the Antiemetic Activity of Cinnamic Acid Targeting 5-HT₃, D₂, and D₃ Receptors in a Copper Sulphate-Induced Chick Model: An In Vivo and In Silico Study"

evidence_items.summary: Analysis code and processed dataset for a market-scale empirical benchmark of 310 European-market production battery electric vehicles, using manufacturer specifications certified under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure (WLTP). CONTENTS The deposit contains the analysis dataset (478 vehicles, of which 310 carry complete certified figures) and four Python scripts that reproduce every table and figure in the accompanying article. Running run all.py regenerates the full set of results in roughly two minutes. WHY THE DATASET CARRIES TWO VARIABLE SETS The upstream specification source publishes both manufacturer-certified type-approval figures and its own modelled estimates of real-world performance. A field-identification audit established that three widely used columns hold the modelled estimates rather than the certified values. The choice is consequential: on the same 310 vehicles, the fleet-level correlation between energy consumption and certified range is -0.31 using certified figures and +0.02 using the modelled estimates, and the multivariate consumption elasticity is -0.886 against -0.393. Both variable sets are retained side by side in certified dataset.csv so this comparison can be reproduced directly. KEY RESULTS REPRODUCED Useable battery capacity is the dominant correlate of certified range, with an almost exactly proportional multivariate elasticity (1.013, 95% CI 0.985 to 1.041). Energy consumption carries a partial elasticity of -0.886. Raw energy consumption differs across drivetrain layouts, but the difference tracks vehicle size and mass and no layout term survives conditioning; the drivetrain result is reported as a bounded null, with any residual association confined to roughly 2% of certified range.

evidence_items.summary: This repository contains the experimental dataset and R scripts generated during the development and optimization of an instant functional beverage powder formulated from cheese whey and Caqueteña pineapple (Ananas comosus L. Merr.) using spray-drying technology. The dataset includes the physicochemical characterization of raw materials (cheese whey and pineapple pulp), formulation design, spray-drying operating conditions, physicochemical and technological properties of the resulting powders, and sensory acceptance data of the reconstituted beverages evaluated by untrained panelists. Measured variables include pH, titratable acidity, density, fat, protein, moisture content, ash, water activity, °Brix, color coordinates (L , a , b ), powder yield, solubility, wettability, and hedonic sensory scores for appearance, color, aroma, body, acidity, and flavor. In addition, this repository provides the R scripts used for statistical analysis, including descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), principal component analysis (PCA), heatmap visualization, and multivariate exploratory modeling. The integration of experimental data and reproducible analytical code provides a reliable computational framework for the study of spray-dried dairy-fruit systems and supports data reuse in food powder engineering, sensory science, multivariate statistics, and sustainable valorisation of agro-industrial by-products.

evidence_items.summary: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Reverse CoT generation (RCG) is cheaper because it conditions on the known answer, but access to this answer can lead to post-hoc rationalization and a mismatch with the student's answer-free inference setting. We propose CoTranslator, which learns to translate reverse CoT responses toward the distribution of verified forward responses. Trained on a small set of paired reverse and rejection-sampled forward responses, it supports large-scale generation and verification of student training data. Across six student models evaluated on six mathematics benchmarks, CoTranslator improves average accuracy over semantic suppression by up to 5.82 percentage points. For two 4B students, it retains 95.0% of rejection sampling's average accuracy while using 35.9% of its estimated compute. Without retraining, the same translator transfers to a new mathematics dataset, a different teacher, and STEM problems, improving average STEM accuracy by 4.88 and 4.31 percentage points for 4B and 8B students, respectively. These results show that CoTranslator offers an efficient and transferable approach to reasoning distillation.
evidence_items.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation

rationale: Matched: benchmark, dataset, evaluat, test set
evidence_items.summary: Video subtitle removal (VSR) is an important video restoration task, yet existing evaluation remains limited by low-resolution datasets, fragmented test sets, and generic video-inpainting protocols that fail to adequately capture localized restoration errors, unintended modifications, temporal instability, and incomplete outputs. In this paper, we introduce MFVSR, a large-scale multi-style benchmark for fine-grained and reliability-aware video subtitle removal evaluation. MFVSR distinguishes itself through three key features: (1) Large-scale and diverse data, comprising 3,000 paired videos from Real-HQ, Real-LQ, and AI-Generated sources, with an auxiliary set of 953 in-the-wild real videos for real-world coverage analysis; (2) Controlled subtitle diversity, spanning 16 languages and four factors covering spatial layout, temporal behavior, visual style, and language mode; (3) Fine-grained evaluation, introducing an information-conditioned, spatially decoupled protocol that separates blind from mask-guided removal and measures Restoration Fidelity, Preservation Fidelity, Temporal Fidelity, coverage, and failures. Experiments on six representative methods reveal substantial discrepancies between local restoration, outside-region preservation, temporal consistency, and full-set reliability that are obscured by conventional full-frame metrics. MFVSR therefore provides a more comprehensive and diagnostic foundation for evaluating and advancing video subtitle removal methods.
evidence_items.title: MFVSR: A Multi-Style and Fine-Grained Benchmark for Video Subtitle Removal

evidence_items.summary: This repository contains two meteorological datasets collected at the Krummendeich Research Wind Farm (WiValdi) by the Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR e.V.). The data includes interpolated vertical profiles from combined mast and remote sensing instruments, alongside surface meteorological observations from a microwave radiometer ground station. Both datasets use a unified time base. Updates in this version: The profile data now includes multiple timestamps (time(6)) instead of a single timestamp. evidence_items.summary: Summary When drilling risks such as kick events occur, rapidly identifying the root causes and recommending effective mitigation measures is critical for well control and operational safety. Traditional incident analysis mainly relies on expert experience and rule-based diagnostics, which are time-consuming and often lack systematic interpretability. This paper proposes a Large Language Model (LLM)-based framework to automatically interpret risk causes and generate mitigation recommendations following drilling risk events. Historical drilling incident reports, operational logs, engineering guidelines, and mitigation case records are first collected to construct a drilling risk knowledge base. A word embedding model is then domain-fine-tuned using drilling-related corpora to enhance semantic representation of domain-specific terminology and operational context. Based on the enhanced embeddings, a knowledge retrieval mechanism identifies relevant historical cases and engineering knowledge. The retrieved knowledge and event descriptions—including drilling parameters and operational records—are provided to a Large Language Model, which performs structured reasoning to interpret possible causes and generate recommended mitigation measures. The proposed framework is evaluated using drilling incident datasets covering 45 wells and 56 recorded risk cases from wells drilled in western China oilfields, together with associated drilling reports and operational documentation. Experimental results show that domain-fine-tuned word embeddings significantly improve semantic retrieval performance, increasing relevant case retrieval accuracy from 0.713 to 0.863. With the enhanced knowledge retrieval, the LLM can effectively identify key contributing factors and produce structured explanations of incident causation.
evidence_items.title: A Large Language Model Framework for Risk Cause Interpretation and Mitigation Recommendation in Drilling Operations

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show promise for clinical decision support but are limited by opaque knowledge and inconsistent decision-making. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates these issues by injecting verifiable passages from a curated corpus at inference time. Using 2,400 real patient pathways from the MIMIC-CDM dataset, we evaluated RAG configurations over information gathering, diagnostic accuracy, treatment recommendations and guideline retrieval, identifying key factors for integrating RAG into clinical AI-agents. Across eight general and medical LLMs spanning 1B to 70B parameters, RAG consistently increased mean diagnostic accuracy from 55.64% to 64.29%, an 8.65-points gain (P=0.0039). In a matched three-backbone analysis, RAG improved physical-examination, imaging and laboratory clinician test-ordering alignment by 5.17 points and treatment alignment by 3.97 points, while surfacing verifiable guideline citations for clinicians. Benefits depended on retrieval design, with autonomous query rewriting producing the clearest effect on retrieval fidelity and downstream performance. These findings demonstrate that guideline-grounded RAG can improve both the outcomes and clinical-decision pathways of LLM-agents while increasing their traceability and transparency.
evidence_items.title: Towards guideline-grounded clinical decision-making: a multi-scale study of retrieval augmented generation based large language model agents

evidence_items.summary: Synthetic data is increasingly used in language-model pretraining. Existing knowledge-corpus synthesis pipelines, including WRAP and Nemotron-CC, usually take a source passage or document segment as input and generate rewritten or QA-style samples from that text. This can improve surface form and prompt diversity, but it does not explicitly require fine-grained source facts -- especially secondary entities, list/table entries, and precise temporal attributes -- to appear in the synthesized corpus. We propose AFCS (Atomic-Fact-Conditioned Synthesis), a pipeline that first extracts source-supported atomic facts and then uses each retained fact to drive generation. AFCS uses structure-aware extraction over the document tree, source-grounded verification, local context expansion, and multi-format generation. In continued-pretraining experiments with OLMo-3-7B and a 32B base on the same FineWiki source corpus, AFCS outperforms WRAP and Nemotron-CC on SimpleQA, SimpleQA Verified, PopQA, and HotpotQA. Granularity ablations show that fact-level synthesis improves over chunk-level, paragraph-level, and entity-level synthesis; and a 100B-token mid-training integration improves factual benchmarks and raises the 12-task general benchmark average by +1.09.
evidence_items.title: AFCS: Atomic-Fact-Conditioned Synthesis for Factual Knowledge Pretraining

evidence_items.summary: Massively multilingual speech modeling has made remarkable progress in recent years, yet existing training resources and benchmarks still underrepresent much of the linguistic long tail. To address this gap, we introduce ELARSpeech, a large-scale multilingual speech resource comprising 30,202 hours of speech across 675 underrepresented languages, curated from the Endangered Languages Archive. Combining human-annotated and unlabeled recordings, the corpus spans diverse recording conditions, domains, and language families. Beyond corpus construction, our experiments show how ELARSpeech supports extending ASR and TTS capabilities to diverse underrepresented languages, with further benefits from pseudo-labeling unlabeled data. At the same time, our speech representation analysis reveals remaining limitations in transferring existing multilingual models to the linguistic long tail. Together, ELARSpeech provides both a resource and a testbed for extending multilingual speech technology further into the linguistic long tail. We publicly release the dataset, all trained ASR and TTS models, and the complete data construction pipeline to facilitate research on long-tail multilingual speech technologies.
evidence_items.title: ELARSpeech: A 30K-Hour Dataset Across 675 Underrepresented Languages for Long-Tail Multilingual Speech Technologies
