evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) particularly machine learning (ML) are increasingly used to predict perioperative risk in patients undergoing major cancer surgery. This narrative review aims to orient perioperative clinicians to contemporary AI-based predictive modelling, critically appraise the current evidence, and examine how these tools can be integrated into clinical decision-making within a Learning Health System framework. Recent studies show promise for AI-based prediction of perioperative outcomes compared with traditional tools in selected settings. However, performance gains are variable. Many models lack explainability, external validation, calibration assessment, or evidence of real-world clinical impact. AI-based predictive models show promise for perioperative risk stratification in cancer surgery, but require external validation, interpretability, and links to actionable clinical pathways to be rigorously established. Future research should prioritise prospective evaluation, equity, workflow integration, and implementation science to translate predictive accuracy into meaningful clinical benefit.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Risk Prediction in Perioperative Cancer Surgery: a Narrative Review

evidence_items.summary:
PURPOSE
To evaluate the efficacy of a computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-based artificial intelligence system for use in the clinical setting to stratify the risk of pulmonary embolism (PE).


MATERIALS AND METHODS
This study enrolled 115 patients diagnosed with PE based on positive CTPA reports at our institution between January 1 and October 10, 2023. Cases were classified as relatively high-risk or low-risk according to the 2019 ESC Guidelines. Two radiologists independently and blindly measured risk-related imaging parameters, including main pulmonary artery diameter (MPAD), ascending aortic diameter (AAD), right and left ventricular diameters (RVD, LVD), the right-to-left ventricular diameter ratio (RVD/LVD ratio), pulmonary artery obstruction index (PAOI), and pulmonary embolism volume (PEV). These results were compared with those from the automated artificial intelligence (AI) system to assess consistency.


RESULTS
The agreement (intraclass correlation coefficients, ICCs) of MPAD, AAD, RVD, PAOI, LVD, and RVD/LVD ratio between AI system and manual measurements were 0.94, 0.79, 0.78, 0.80, 0.54, and 0.48, respectively. Among the AI-extracted covariates, an RVD/LVD ratio >1.2 showed good performance in identifying relatively high-risk PE cases, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.771. The AI model incorporating all covariates achieved an AUC of 0.848 for classifying high-risk PE.


CONCLUSIONS
The CTPA-based AI system can rapidly extract the key imaging parameters relevant to PE risk stratification in real-world clinical settings, significantly reducing the CTPA interpretation time and improving evaluation efficiency.
evidence_items.title: A Real-World Clinical Study on Computed Tomography Pulmonary Angiography-Based Artificial Intelligence-Driven Risk Stratification in Pulmonary Embolism.

evidence_items.summary: As Internet of Things (IoT) devices collect and process data, security is essential. IoT devices often combine with other emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and fifth-generation (5G) communications, to support applications such as smart grids and internet-of-vehicles (IoV). Because IoT devices are deployed remotely, remote attestation (RA) effectively verifies each device's state. However, the scale of IoT deployments makes device management challenging for owners. Therefore, cloud-assisted IoT management services often provide RA solutions. Although cloud-based IoT services can securely manage IoT devices, passive malicious administrators or hacked IoT device owners'accounts can control IoT devices without cloud IoT service authorization. Therefore, this work proposes a cloud-assisted RA system that addresses three main challenges of IoT device RA: 1) lightweight RA design for resource-limited IoT devices, 2) unauthorized access to IoT devices by passive malicious administrators or compromised owner accounts on the cloud IoT management platform, and 3) RA may not extend to an authenticated key exchange protocol. In addition to proposing a swarm RA scheme that addresses these three challenges, this work analyzes the system's security properties and evaluates its feasibility through implementation and simulation.
evidence_items.title: ESAU: Expeditious Swarm Remote Attestation for Pub-Sub IoT Networks with Untrusted Cloud-based Proxy Verifier

evidence_items.summary: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut. POCUS in OB/GYN is a focused clinical examination for immediate decision-making, not a substitute for comprehensive diagnostic ultrasound. The strongest current evidence supports early pregnancy triage, fetal viability and presentation, selected intrapartum questions, and pragmatic gynecologic triage. Handheld devices, AI-enabled blind sweeps and tele-ultrasound have expanded the practical reach of POCUS, especially outside tertiary ultrasound units. Implementation requires a governance model: indications, training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection and escalation pathways. The curriculum, credentialing model and governance framework proposed in this review are an expert-informed proposal intended for discussion and local adaptation, not a formally validated or consensus-based European standard. evidence_items.summary: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/
evidence_items.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture

evidence_items.summary: World and action modeling are closely related, yet their reciprocal benefits under unified causal training remain unclear. We introduce OneWM, a simple framework for unified causal training that treats actions as both conditions for world prediction and targets for policy learning within a shared video-action architecture. Using this framework, we investigate whether learning forward dynamics conditioned on specified actions improves action learning, and whether learning to generate actions in turn improves action-conditioned world modeling. We use LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa365 as embodied testbeds to evaluate both policy learning and world modeling, complemented by real-world policy experiments. Learning the visual consequences of specified actions improves policy performance and generalization across changing scenes. In turn, action learning improves multi-view world-prediction fidelity under the same architecture. Together, these results answer both questions positively, supporting reciprocal benefits between world modeling and action generation under unified causal training.
evidence_items.title: Can World and Action Modeling Benefit Each Other under Unified Causal Training?

evidence_items.summary: Policy-shift distillation reuses the difference between a teacher's log probabilities before and after reinforcement learning (RL) as supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, this endpoint policy shift cannot reveal whether local action preferences evolved consistently during teacher training. The same endpoint shift can result from early and late shifts that reinforce or partially cancel each other. We investigate whether agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts can guide selective transfer. We introduce Waypoint-guided On-Policy Distillation (Waypoint-OPD), which uses an intermediate teacher checkpoint from the same RL run to compare early and late shifts in relative action preferences at student-visited prefixes. We gate the endpoint shift according to the directional agreement between the early and late shifts, suppressing it when they point in opposing directions. Compared with endpoint-only transfer, our method requires only one additional frozen-teacher scoring pass. Using RL-trained Qwen3-4B teachers, we evaluate our method with Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B as student models in mathematical and code reasoning. In all six domain--student settings, Waypoint-OPD achieves the highest domain-average score among the compared distillation methods. Ablations with the Qwen3-8B student show that removing or shuffling gates reduces mathematical reasoning performance. These results support the use of directional agreement between early and late teacher policy shifts to weight the endpoint shift during student training.
evidence_items.title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
evidence_items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering

evidence_items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. This paper proposes Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation (SCOPED), which trains capability-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection. During on-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill-decoupled on-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student. All code and data are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/SCOPED.
evidence_items.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.
evidence_items.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos

evidence_items.summary: Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design a data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires. We first run this loop with a single agent, and it reaches only one action, adjusting category proportions, while its context fills with execution output and is discarded mid-search. We therefore introduce AutoSFT, a multi-agent system where a meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls a synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by +6.5, and synthesis adds +3.4 IFEval and +2.9 IFBench. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds +3.7 MBPP+ over a single agent that does not improve. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each component's effect is individually attributable. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on a stronger single action.
evidence_items.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning

evidence_items.summary: Long-output inference in large language models suffers from severe KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. While KV cache quantization alleviates this issue, low-bit quantization (e.g., 2-bit) severely degrades model accuracy. Recent mixed-precision key-cache quantization methods mitigate this degradation by allocating higher precision to important key channels, but estimate channel saliency using only key statistics. Through attention logit perturbation analysis at the RoPE channel-pair level, we show that quantization errors in channel pairs with large query--key pair-norm products contribute significantly to logit variation. Based on this insight, we propose PN-Mix, a mixed-precision key-cache quantization method for RoPE-based decoder-only LLMs, which allocates higher precision to salient channel pairs identified once during the prefill stage and reused throughout decoding. Across standard reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks, PN-Mix with 2.26-bit average precision achieves comparable or better average accuracy than prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32--2.39 bits. Furthermore, in our Pareto sweep, PN-Mix degrades gracefully down to 1.5 bits, whereas the compared baselines exhibit sharper performance drops below 2.25 bits.
evidence_items.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference

evidence_items.summary: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.
evidence_items.title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution

evidence_items.summary: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. We present Intern Lumina U2, to our knowledge the first diffusion language model to represent multi-codebook visual tokens in a fully discrete space. Each visual position is represented by a group of codes from complementary codebooks, increasing its representational capacity while preserving compatibility with discrete text modeling. At the input, the embeddings are concatenated at each position; at the output, a lightweight multi-codebook autoregressive head predicts the codes within each position sequentially, while the diffusion backbone processes all positions in parallel. Built on the unified 4D representation of AToken, Intern Lumina U2 supports image, video, and 3D inputs within a single backbone and achieves leading performance among unified models in visual understanding, image generation, and image editing. We further build a full-stack training, inference, and evaluation system on both Ascend and NVIDIA platforms to verify the cross-platform effectiveness of our model. We also improve the inference efficiency through a stability-aware sampling strategy, which combines confidence-plateau-guided unmasking approach with drift-triggered cache refreshing mechanisms, accelerating image generation by 4.45x.
evidence_items.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation

evidence_items.summary: Recent work has explored visual reasoning through image generation, where models solve visual-reasoning problems by directly generating solution images. Intuitively, iterative samplers such as flow matching are well suited to this task, since each sampling step may resemble one reasoning step. However, in this work, from a circuit complexity perspective, we show that this intuition is misleading. We prove that as long as the model outputs satisfy certain mild regularity conditions, the trajectory of the vanilla flow-matching sampler can be simulated by a constant number of sequential rounds of parallel model evaluations. Consequently, additional sampling steps cannot increase the expressive power of a constant-depth backbone model under the standard complexity-theoretic model of transformers. We then reveal that self-conditioning, which conditions the model on the previous step's estimate of the final image, plays a previously unrecognized role in removing this bottleneck. Controlled experiments on diverse visual-reasoning tasks show that flow matching with self-conditioning achieves higher accuracy and greater reasoning depth than vanilla flow matching, and its performance improves with more sampling steps. Theoretically, we prove that with self-conditioning, a constant-depth backbone can achieve expressive power equivalent to that of space-bounded Turing machines. Our study suggests a design principle for future visual reasoning research: carry more information between sampling steps, so that additional steps translate into deeper reasoning.
evidence_items.title: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching

evidence_items.summary: Monocular world-space human recovery methods excel on current benchmarks, but these rarely include fast camera motion. We introduce the K-Pop stress test, broadcast dance videos that combine fast, large camera motion with dense multi-person choreography. Leading methods produce plausible per-frame meshes on these videos, yet their world-space trajectories drift far from the performers' stage positions. Through a systematic diagnosis, we show that the camera and human estimates each remain self-consistent, and that the drift appears when they are combined at mismatched scales. Each is recovered at its own scale, so a mismatch between the two can turn camera motion into human drift that grows with camera displacement and becomes severe in broadcast dance videos. We derive a closed-form correction that estimates this mismatch and applies one scale to all performers, removing the drift while keeping their relative positions in one shared world frame. It requires no retraining and works with existing backends. Combined with physical constraints, the correction yields stable world-space reconstruction for choreography modeling, scene editing, data generation, and virtual reshooting.
evidence_items.title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics

evidence_items.summary: Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn. Existing environment-generation pipelines largely optimize generic properties such as realism, diversity, or task coverage, while different pretrained policies can fail for different environmental reasons. We therefore introduce WEDGE, a framework for weakness-guided navigation learning in which the failure modes of a pretrained agent guide the generation of training environments at each adaptation round. Given a pretrained policy, WEDGE uses an LLM to propose executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, automatically validates them on the diagnostic set, and selects the strongest validated weakness based on its success-rate gap. The validated weaknesses are then mapped to the environmental factors that control them. WEDGE varies these factors to construct environments in the difficulty regimes where the policy struggles, producing targeted training experience for adaptation. Across three navigation agents with different adaptation mechanisms, we find that policies exhibit distinct weakness profiles and benefit from different training environments. Weakness-conditioned adaptation consistently outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR, while the resulting gains for Uni-NaVid and Gemini also extend to HM3D after ProcTHOR adaptation. Iterative re-diagnosis further shows that dominant weaknesses can persist or shift as the policy improves, providing updated guidance for subsequent environment construction. Together, these results show that policy failures are not only diagnostic signals, but actionable guidance for constructing training environments that target a policy's current weaknesses.
evidence_items.title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents

evidence_items.summary: Current video object removal methods suffer from prohibitive latency (minutes per video) and non-causal processing that prevents real-time interaction. We present StreamErase, enabling sub-second latency with up to 26 FPS streaming generation on a single GPU. Our approach first augments a text-to-video model with mask input to generate high-quality videos that erase target objects and synthesize coherent backgrounds, but does not perform inference on the fly. As such, we progressively transfer the erasing capability from a powerful bidirectional foundation model to an efficient unidirectional streaming eraser, enabling long-horizon erasing without sacrificing visual fidelity. Several key challenges arise when generating videos over long, potentially infinite horizons: (1) bridging the domain gap from training on finite length and extrapolating to long horizons, (2) sustaining high quality by preventing error accumulation, and (3) maintaining fast inference, without increasing computational cost as the context grows. To address these challenges, we carefully designed sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks. By incorporating self-rollout with attention sinks and KV cache rolling during training, we simulate inference-time extrapolations with a fixed context window, enabling constant-speed generation of arbitrarily long videos. Finally, we establish a dedicated benchmark, LongErase, for streaming long-video object removal. Our model achieves strong performance compared to existing video object erasing models and generalizes well to real-world video scenarios, uniquely enabling infinite-length streaming. With StreamErase, users can input a mask and see the erasing results unfold in real-time, delivering a truly interactive experience.
evidence_items.title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing

evidence_items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program scores can hide components useful to other agents. To address these challenges, we introduce SwarmRSI, a framework that evolves scientific agent swarms for recursive self-improvement. We devise Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and their implementations using experimental feedback from other agents. We also propose Complementary Swarm Recombination to reuse retained hypotheses and complementary program components across agents, allowing partial results to support new research. Recursive Swarm Evolution integrates both mechanisms into a feedback loop, using new experimental evidence to guide subsequent research. Experiments on OpenProblems, NatureBench and MLE-Bench Lite demonstrate SwarmRSI's state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. Further evaluations show that accumulated research experience improves performance on held-out tasks. Biologists also reproduce its programs for follow-up biological analyses.
evidence_items.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm

evidence_items.summary: Evaluation for automatic crisis reporting should measure what practitioners need, not what is convenient to compare. Through LLM-assisted, author-approved content analysis, we derive a 15-slot information schema from professional humanitarian situation reports using qualitative content analysis, then evaluate 121 human and 261 LLM-generated reports across five disasters and three hazard types. Under google/gemini-3.7-flash on Cyclone Idai, the best machine arm is nominally above the empirical human ceiling (0.827 vs. 0.821), but the difference is statistically indistinguishable from zero (95\% bootstrap CI [-.049,.059]; permutation p=.852), and the ordering does not replicate under openai/gpt-5.6-luna. On a blind 100-item Idai sample, the author agrees with the Gemini judge at 0.910 accuracy and unweighted Cohen's κ=.799. All four judges clear the plan's raw-agreement criterion of .7; only Gemini reaches .7 on chance-corrected κ. Across the three primary events, machine reports reproduce 5.4-11.0% of same-day official figures. Across those same events, raw exact-number matching links 14.3-19.6% of official figures and 85.4-90.1% of machine figures to the social stream; manual audit confirms 45/50 declared absences, 4/25 official matches, and 24/25 machine matches semantically. The issuing-provenance gap is positive in all 12 observed event-judge cells: report date, organisation, series, and authority were not supplied at professional-report coverage in any cell. On the three primary events, ROUGE-L is uninformative, BERTScore is negatively associated with completeness after multiplicity correction, and a generic LLM judge changes sign.
evidence_items.title: Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports

evidence_items.summary: Training-free diffusion-based compression methods repurpose the generative priors of a diffusion or a flow model to compress data without retraining them as task-specific codecs. Recent codebook-based approaches such as Turbo-DDCM achieve strong perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates, but their reliance on dense Gaussian codebooks remains costly in both memory and computation, and scales poorly with the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators. Their combinatorial bitstream encoding further becomes computationally heavy at this scale. We introduce H-DDCM, a scalable generative compression framework that replaces Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries. The fast Walsh-Hadamard transform allows for implicitly synthesizing full-dimensional dictionaries with O(d log d) compute for projection and reconstruction and O(d) memory, without materializing the full-dimensional dictionary. We further introduce an efficient table-free lexicographic coding scheme that makes combinatorial encoding practical at larger dimensions. Beyond images, we adapt the framework to an autoregressive video flow model and develop a streaming compression scheme that periodically re-encodes recently reconstructed frames into a fresh KV-cache prefix, preserving temporal context across segments at no additional transmitted bits. This enables long-form, close to real-time generative video compression on a single GPU. Across image and video benchmarks, H-DDCM achieves competitive rate-distortion-perception performance while substantially reducing the memory and computational overhead of codebook-based training-free generative compression.
evidence_items.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression

evidence_items.summary: Can a vision-language model tell left from right? Modern VLMs solve visual puzzles and follow hour-long videos, yet when asked whether the camera moved left or right, most do no better than a coin flip. Adding camera-motion data or geometric representations has been tried, separately, and neither closes the gap. We argue that camera-motion understanding needs two conditions at once: the representation must couple off-screen camera motion with on-screen flow dynamics, and it must be interpreted by the language model rather than trained as a standalone pose or depth estimator. We propose CameraVLM, which pairs a motion-state representation with state-language alignment. Camera tokens capture how the camera moves off screen, flow tokens capture how the subject and background move on screen, and a two-stage training strategy keeps language in the loop so that both are learned together with camera-motion semantics. With only 9B parameters, CameraVLM outperforms all open-source and camera-motion-specific models by a wide margin across three benchmarks and more than 20 baselines, and matches or surpasses GPT-6 Astra as well as human viewers in a 48-participant study. Project page: https://3dagentworld.github.io/CameraVLM/
evidence_items.title: When Left Is Right? Camera-Motion Understanding beyond Screen

evidence_items.summary: Driving world action models (WAMs) learn from paired trajectories and future observations. Post-training with reinforcement learning allows the policy to explore alternative trajectories and improve planning using driving rewards. However, driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectories, leaving these alternatives without corresponding visual supervision. Thus, we introduce SimVTA, a simulation-grounded post-training framework that combines trajectory optimization with video supervision. First, we sample candidate trajectories for each observation and use a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) to render future videos for high-reward candidates in real-world scenes reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). This provides trajectory-matched supervision independent of the model's own predictions. Under a limited rendering budget, we prioritize video supervision for higher-error futures among these rendered candidates. Finally, we optimize trajectory planning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and use a flow-matching loss on the matched videos to update shared representations. At inference time, the model predicts trajectories directly, without simulator calls. On NAVSIM v1, applying SimVTA to a WAM initialization improves PDMS from 86.2 to 91.3 (+5.1). It achieves 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 38.8 in closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM. Ablations show that updating shared representations with video supervision improves planning, while prioritizing higher-error futures among high-reward trajectories further improves performance.
evidence_items.title: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models

evidence_items.summary:
Coding agents such as Claude Code also follow text files that developers write for them: a project file, skills the agent may choose to open, and rules that load automatically when the agent reads matching files. We call these files the agent's harness. Developers add to it whenever they correct the agent, but one success proves little: the same agent can pass a task once and fail it the next time.
  We present Cortex, a tool that tests changes to the harness instead of trusting them. It saves fixes from the developer's sessions as replayable tasks, finds the corrections that recur, writes one skill or rule at a time, and keeps it only if repeated runs with and without it show a net gain and no task made noticeably worse. Existing text is tested the same way before it is deleted, and Cortex neither adds nor deletes text the agent never used.
  We tested Cortex with Claude Haiku 4.5 on a repository built for the purpose, with conventions the model tends to break, one area with nothing to learn, and a script playing the developer. On held-out tasks, the harnesses it built made the agent follow the conventions far more often than no skills or rules did, left the comparison area unchanged, and added no text read on every turn. Rules, which load automatically, did most of the work; skills helped only when offered with the files a task touches, and those offered on every turn were rarely opened. Cortex kept none of the useless or harmful suggestions we planted, but the agent never opened the useless ones or the harmful skills, and it reached no verdict on the harmful rules, so the test shows that Cortex keeps no unused text, not that it detects damage. Under the stronger Claude Sonnet 5 a single run's harness added little, and on a real open-source project, where the agent was rarely corrected, Cortex found nothing to learn. We release the tool, the lab and its data.
evidence_items.title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules

evidence_items.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models have become a leading approach to real-time interactive video generation and video world modeling. However, existing methods typically allocate computation uniformly across space when generating the next video chunk, updating all patches with the same denoising schedule and number of function evaluations. This ignores the spatial heterogeneity of video content: static, simple, or recurring regions are often easier to denoise, while other regions require further refinement or additional context. A uniform budget thus leads to redundant computation on easy patches, whereas reducing the fixed step count can leave difficult patches insufficiently refined. We introduce , a general framework that dynamically allocates denoising steps to individual patches: easy patches stop early to improve efficiency, while difficult patches receive more refinement steps. This design accelerates generation with negligible quality degradation. Our method is compatible with most existing few-step autoregressive diffusion models, requiring only a lightweight routing module with modest training. Experiments demonstrate that  reduces the total number of denoising steps applied across video patches by about 50\% while maintaining visual quality comparable to the four-step baseline.
evidence_items.title: ForcingBooster: Adaptive Patch-wise Denoising for Fast Autoregressive Video Diffusion

evidence_items.summary: Post-route power recovery changes cell choices under tightly coupled timing, electrical and physical constraints, and the value of each change depends on what it costs to repair its side effects. We propose an AI-driven framework in which a learned model drives both phases of the optimization: it ranks the powerrecovery edits to try and the repair actions that follow, while deterministic electronic design automation (EDA) analyses govern every acceptance. The framework records baseline constraint margins, identifies the damage a recovery transaction introduces in each analysis view, holds pre-existing violations at their baseline rather than working them inside the power step, and caps repair spending at a fraction of the measured saving. An ensemble of gradient-boosted models predicts power change, normalized damage reduction and constraint-regression risk from action and timing-context features available before each trial; calibrated, conservative estimates feed separate acquisition scores for recovery and repair, with a deterministic fallback when the model is uncertain. Recovery and repair remain speculative until physical implementation and fresh analysis establish baseline preservation and positive net saving. We specify the contract, the learned policy, the transactional flow and a pre-registered public evaluation protocol on open designs. Evidence from a companion study on public designs supports the contract; the learned policy is proposed, and no trained-model results or proprietary design measurements are reported.
evidence_items.title: AI-Driven, Timing-Aware Power Optimization

evidence_items.summary: Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.
evidence_items.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?

evidence_items.summary: Most vision-language-action models represent future motion as fixed-rate action chunks, tying temporal resolution and prediction horizon to a fixed output budget. This pointwise representation wastes capacity on highly correlated neighboring actions, leaves temporal continuity and smoothness to be learned implicitly, and forces a tradeoff between long-horizon coverage and the local precision required for contact-rich manipulation. To address these limitations, we introduce Vela, a vision-language-action foundation model that represents future robot behavior as continuous trajectories. Vela combines a compact spline-based action representation with motion-dependent temporal support and a shared action interface for heterogeneous embodiments, allowing a fixed output budget to adapt its temporal resolution across motions. We pretrain Vela on large-scale multi-embodiment robot data and evaluate it on LIBERO-X, EBench, and two real-world long-horizon tasks, egg-cake cooking and potato shredding, obtaining promising results across simulation and physical manipulation. These results highlight the potential of continuous action representations as a foundation for future embodied foundation models. Project page and more results: https://clementine24.github.io/Vela/ .
evidence_items.title: Vela: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Adaptive Action Curve Parametrization

answers.counter_view: These are newly released, author-described artifacts rather than independent validations. Broader scenarios can add substantial evaluation cost without improving decisions if they do not match the intended deployment, so teams should not adopt the entire set merely because the captured feed highlights it.
answers.counter_view_zh: 这些是新发布且由作者自行描述的项目，并非独立验证结果。如果更广泛的场景与预期部署不匹配，就可能大幅增加评估成本，却无法改善决策。因此，团队不应仅因本次抓取的信息流突出展示了这些项目，就全盘采用。
answers.plain_chinese: 增加一条贴近实际部署的专项测试线。纳入不明确的请求、由相互依赖工作组成的长序列、人工交接、过时或相互冲突的证据，以及通过工具接触到的恶意内容。仅试点与自身系统相关的场景，并保留现有测试以供比较。
answers.plain_english: Add a focused test lane that resembles your deployment. Include unclear requests, long sequences of dependent work, human handoffs, stale or conflicting evidence, and hostile content encountered through tools. Pilot only scenarios relevant to your system, and keep existing tests for comparison.
answers.question: What should someone building or evaluating AI systems do differently today?
answers.signal: In this keyword-filtered feed, benchmark and agentic observations are higher across the recent comparable window, while new releases emphasize deployment-shaped evaluation: ambiguous requirements, dependent tasks, human collaboration, unsafe external instructions, and uncertain workflow states.
answers.signal_zh: 在该关键词过滤信息流中，近期可比时间窗口内的基准和智能体相关观测量更高；与此同时，新发布项目更强调贴近部署情境的评估，包括模糊需求、相互依赖的任务、人机协作、不安全的外部指令，以及不确定的工作流状态。
answers.takeaway: Treat standard benchmark scores as one layer rather than the whole evaluation. Prioritize failures that could change system actions, escalation decisions, or user outcomes, and record reliability and operating cost alongside task success.
answers.takeaway_zh: 应将标准基准分数视为评估的一个层面，而不是评估的全部。优先关注可能改变系统行动、升级处置决策或用户结果的失效，并在记录任务成功情况的同时，记录可靠性和运行成本。

answers.counter_view: Some records were independently sighted by more than one source, which increases confidence that the artifacts exist and were noticed. However, independent discovery does not mean that multiple sources reproduced the benchmark results or measured the same usage metric.
answers.counter_view_zh: 一些记录被不止一个来源独立观测到，这提高了对相关项目确实存在且受到关注的信心。然而，独立发现并不意味着多个来源复现了基准结果，也不意味着它们测量了同一项使用指标。
answers.plain_chinese: 发布公告描述的是作者声称自己构建了什么；它不能证明其他团队可以复现结果，也不能证明更高的分数会带来更好的现实结果。关注度和下载量反映的是可见度或访问情况，而不是质量、采用程度或有效性。
answers.plain_english: A release announcement describes what authors say they built; it does not show that another team can reproduce the results or that better scores lead to better real-world outcomes. Attention and downloads indicate visibility or access, not quality, adoption, or effectiveness.
answers.question: What does today's evidence fail to show, and what would change the reading?
answers.signal: The captured feed does not establish that newly released benchmarks are representative, reproducible, or predictive of deployment performance. The listed download movements are cumulative across each artifact’s full tracked span, not daily changes, and each comes from a single source rather than corroborated measurement.
answers.signal_zh: 本次抓取的信息流无法证明新发布的基准具有代表性、可复现性，或能够预测部署表现。所列下载量变动均为各项目完整跟踪周期内的累计变化，而非每日变化；并且每项数据均来自单一来源，而非经过交叉验证的测量。
answers.takeaway: The reading would strengthen with independent reruns, third-party baseline results, leakage and contamination audits, versioned data and harnesses, deployment-linked validation, and the same movement metric reported by multiple sources. Broader connector coverage would also reduce dependence on the currently captured feed.
answers.takeaway_zh: 如果能补充独立复跑、第三方基线结果、泄漏与污染审计、带版本的数据和测试框架、与部署关联的验证，以及由多个来源报告的同一种变动指标，相关解读会更有说服力。扩大连接器覆盖范围，也能降低对当前抓取信息流的依赖。
